notes:
I don't have any notes on Ecclesiastes 3 for you yet. My attempts to open the source pages didn't work, and I've reached my tool limit for this turn.

- **What happened:** I tried to load six pages at once: the Enduring Word chapter commentary, the Precept Austin chapter page, and the Bible Hub commentary pages for verses 1, 11, 15 and 21. The tool returned data in a different format than expected, so I couldn't read any page text. When I retried, the request went over the usage limit, and a search I tried after that was also blocked.
- **Why there are no notes:** Your rules say to report only what pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read no pages, any verse notes I wrote now would be made up.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll start with the pages that cover the most ground, one or two at a time so a failure doesn't waste the rest:

1. **Verse-by-verse traditional reading:** Enduring Word on Ecclesiastes 3, Precept Austin's chapter commentary, and the Bible Hub pages for each verse (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and others).
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** likely candidates are v. 11 ("eternity in the hearts of men"), v. 14 (what God does and fearing Him), v. 15 (God calling the past to account), and vv. 18–21 (man and beasts, and the spirit after death). I'd check teachers from Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Wesley Center, 1517 and LCMS.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes on vv. 11 and 21, any Bible Odyssey article on Ecclesiastes or Qoheleth, and Catholic or Orthodox material from New Advent and Catholic.com. For prosperity or word-of-faith readings of vv. 1–8 and 12–13, I'll look at GotQuestions and The Gospel Coalition, and include them only if the pages actually discuss them.
